title: Projectile Target Challenge: Pick Angle and Speed
description: A launcher sits at the left end of a flat 70 m field with marks every 10 m. A red target disc with a flag is placed down the field. Set the launch angle and speed, then press Launch: the orange ball flies along its arc, leaving a trail. Your previous arc stays as a faded line. Readouts show the landing distance, the miss distance, whether the shot was short, long or a hit, the flight time, the highest point, launches used and targets hit. Hit 3 targets (30 m, 45 m, 18 m) within 10 launches.

game.objective: Hit 3 targets in turn (30 m, 45 m, then 18 m) using no more than 10 launches. A hit lands within 1.5 m of the target's centre.
game.hint: At the same speed, angles that add up to 90° (like 30° and 60°) land at the same distance, and 45° goes farthest. Doubling the speed makes the shot go four times as far.

assumptions: This is a simplified simulation: no air resistance, and the ball starts at ground level on flat ground.
Gravity is 9.8 m/s² straight down. The ball keeps the same sideways speed; only its vertical speed changes.
Each frame of the flight is computed exactly from the projectile formulas, so the landing distance equals speed² × sin(2 × angle) ÷ 9.8.
The ball is treated as a point for the physics (drawn as a sphere resting on that point); the flight ends when it returns to ground height.
A hit means the landing is within 1.5 m of the target centre, both edges counted; the red disc has exactly that 1.5 m radius.
Targets come in a fixed order (30 m, 45 m, 18 m). Reset starts the same challenge again and clears the score and the arcs.
Each flight is shown over two seconds of screen time whatever its real flight time, so the screen time does not match the flight-time readout.
Real balls are slowed by air and land shorter than shown, especially at high speed. The longest shot here is about 64 m (25 m/s at 45°).
